_comment: REQUIRED BY DEFAULT. A registered type binds on EVERY action unless an entry says otherwise, and saying otherwise costs a stated `reason`. The minimal entry {"family": "..."} is the STRICT one -- adding a type is one line and it binds immediately. Inclusion is free; exclusion is the thing that takes effort.
_why: The first draft listed required steps explicitly per action, so adding a checker meant writing it AND remembering to add it to the list. Forget the second half and the checker runs, passes, and counts for nothing -- absence rendering as success, in the very file that defines what complete means. A registry you must remember to extend is a registry that will be incomplete.
_reasonless_narrowing: An `actions` or `when` narrowing with NO `reason` is IGNORED and the type falls back to required-for-all. This is the encoding_whitelist.txt convention, reused deliberately because it is already familiar here: nothing is suppressed until a human has actually looked. A typo in an exemption fails safe.
_unregistered: V8 rejects a record whose step is not listed here, record.py returns None, and the checker exits 2 -- so the pipeline blocks the moment someone wires in an unregistered check, loudly, at the desk of the person who can fix it. That is the pair that closes the hole: you cannot add a check that silently does not count, and you cannot register one that silently is not required.

prior_art._registered_is_not_admitted: ⚠⚠ `actions: ["push"]` HERE DOES NOT GATE A PUSH, AND THAT SPLIT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS IS SAFE. This file is the REGISTRY -- what may be recorded and what a step is ABOUT. `admission.v1.json` is the ADMISSION SET -- what gitRobot requires green before it lets an action through, defaulting to NOT_ADMITTING. `prior_art` is registered for push and is deliberately ABSENT from admission, so it renders in the 'registered but not gating' line every run and blocks nothing at the ledger. ⚠ MEASURED 2026-09-01, twice, because the first fix was wrong: `coverage_gap` returns `steps: []` for a step that does not apply to the ACTION, and adding `scope` alone did NOT change that -- verified by calling it. A step must apply to the action before the ledger will emit a row for it, and the row is what `batch.check_prior_art_attribution` reads. So `actions` is required for the row to EXIST and `admission.v1.json` is what decides whether it BLOCKS; those were conflated in the revert of the corpus-wide promotion, which removed both and left the push leg unable to ask.
prior_art._scope_and_actions_are_different_jobs: `scope` says WHICH PATHS the step is about and keeps its records file-keyed. `actions` says WHICH ACTIONS it is evaluated for. The corpus-wide promotion of 2026-09-01 set both, was measured backwards (see `_reengaged` below), and was reverted by removing both -- which also removed the input `batch.check_prior_art_attribution` reads. Measured by /rely the same day: with no scope the leg gets `None` from `owing_paths`, correctly fails closed, and blocks EVERY push editing any `.lean` file, naming the wrong cause. Every layer behaved correctly and the composition did not. So: scope YES (the ledger must emit the row and keep the records file-keyed), actions NO (the ledger must not gate on a corpus-wide backlog). The per-file enforcement is the push leg, and it INTERSECTS this scope with the changed set, so the 215-file backlog `coverage_gap` reports is never demanded by anything.
prior_art._reengaged_2026_09_01: RE-ENGAGED under the first clause of `reason` below -- 're-engaged when .lean files are next touched' -- by Tim's decision. ⚠⚠ ENFORCED, BUT NOT FROM HERE, SO `actions: []` NO LONGER MEANS 'DISCIPLINE'. The obligation is now a BLOCKING push leg: `batch.check_prior_art_attribution` requires every `.lean` file a push EDITS to carry a passing `prior_art` verdict at its current bytes. Tim, 2026-09-01: 'whenever a specific file gets edited that that file is properly attributed. the current logic I think hits the entire corpus. and that is impossible to fill at one time.' ⚠ MEASURED WHY IT IS NOT A `scope` HERE: promoting this entry with `scope: ZeroParadox/*.lean` was tried the same day and is backwards on both counts -- it reports `have 3 / missing 215`, an impossible-looking backlog that does NOT block (narrowed coverage is reported, never enforced), while the only thing that DID block was an unrelated recorded FAIL, so a tooling push with no `.lean` in it was refused for a corpus finding. Until then the type stays registered so records remain valid and file-keyed, which is what the leg reads.

agent_gate.reason: ADVISORY interpretation layer - it RECORDS but must never GATE. agent_gate.run() always returns 0 and batch.py deliberately does not increment `bad`, because the layer is fuzzy: measured 2026-08-21 before adoption, 1 false positive in 6 healthy runs, and byte-identical input returned TRUSTWORTHY twice and NOT_TRUSTWORTHY once. The >=2-of-3 vote takes that to 0 but the variance is real, and blocking on a coin flip is how a gate earns itself a bypass (CLAUDE.md rung 5: the screen may replace the enumeration, never the verdict). It is registered so that a CLEAN run leaves a record - verdictLedger.md section 2, 'a step that passes MUST emit a record; silence is never a pass' - which names this file as the measured instance of the defect. Its verdict is honest (it records what it found) and its status is non-gating, which is the registry/admission split working as designed.

check_fields.reason: ADVISORY reading list, registered so it can RECORD but gating nothing. _approved_modules: ⛔⛔ WHICH BUILD MAY RECORD, not merely which file. `module` pins the PATH, so an EDITED checker records exactly as readily as a reviewed one. `approved_modules` lists the blob ids this step accepts, and verdictLedger's V16c REFUSES a record whose `evidence` names an unapproved build. Pinned for PUSH-GATING steps ONLY -- advisory and commit-only steps stay unpinned, so the friction is paid where publication is decided and nowhere else. ⛔⛔ WHEN A CHECKER GETS A NEW BUILD, **REPLACE** THE HASH -- DO NOT ADD TO THE LIST. `["<new>"]` is correct; `["<old>", "<new>"]` is wrong absent a stated expiry. ⚠⚠ AN ACCUMULATING LIST STOPS BEING A PIN: approve v1, v2, v3, v4 and eventually every build ever written is approved -- still LOOKING pinned while constraining nothing. That is `RLY31-6`'s exact shape, where a control decayed into permissiveness while appearing to hold and nothing was positioned to notice; this is the same trap in a different field. The history is already versioned, so every past approved set is recoverable from this file's own log -- a list inside the field duplicates that, and the duplicate is the copy that rots. Old records need no entry either: nothing re-validates the stored stream (`validate` runs only at append), so a record made under v1 stays exactly as valid as the day it landed. THE ONLY LEGITIMATE PAIR IS A ROLLOUT WINDOW -- v2 shipping while a run is in flight on v1 -- and it needs a STATED EXPIRY the way `copy_editor`'s `_why_not_admitted_yet` does, or the transitional pair quietly becomes permanent. ⭐ THE TWO-STEP COST IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS, and this was measured in the server's `inventory.py` rather than assumed: EDITING A CHECKER ALREADY STALES EVERY ROW IT PRODUCED, pinned or not -- `ev_stale` compares each record's `evidence` against current content and reports that the producer changed. So a new build means re-running that step regardless of `approved_modules`, and approving the new blob is ONE LINE IN THE SAME COMMIT THAT SHIPS THE CODE, inside a re-run you already owe. Tim's ruling on the trade: "the 'silently can't record' is the problem. fail loudly." V16c refuses naming BOTH the rejected blob and this field, and approving is a REVIEWABLE EDIT in the same history as the tool change -- the point of pinning rather than an obstacle to it. ⚠ A step with NO `approved_modules` still records; `policy()` reports `unpinned_modules`, so an unpinned step is DISCLOSED rather than silently permitted. ⚠⚠ EVERY BLOB BELOW WAS RE-DERIVED IN THIS TREE with `record.module_evidence`, the same function that computes evidence at record time, and NOT pasted from the message that proposed them. Pinning a stale blob refuses the very next run of that checker, so a copied list is the one thing this field must never contain. ⚠ THE STEP NAME IS NOT THE FILE NAME: `claim_review` pins `check_frozen.py` and `decls` pins `batch.py`. This entry's own `module` is the authority for that mapping. ⚠ IF YOU ADD A REGISTRY KEY AND IT SEEMS IGNORED: the server's `Config.requirements()` rebuilds each spec key by key from a whitelist rather than passing the entry through, so a key absent from that whitelist is invisible to every rule downstream no matter what this file says.
